newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cossack, Griffin fields stop output on weather.
newsitem.headline: Cossack, Griffin fields stop output on weather.

text.p: Australia's Cossack and Griffin oil fields stopped production earlier on Wednesday as bad weather threatened the sites, market sources said.
Cossack was producing about 65,000 barrels per day (bpd) owing to a technical problem with a gas dehydration problem that has required a temporary repair pending replacement parts.
Normal production has been about 80/90,000 bpd although the field is designed to produce above 100,000 bpd.
Griffin was producing at around 80,000 bpd, in line with normal production rates.
Both fields were watching a tropical low formation about 100 nautical miles off the two fields.
Tropical lows can turn into cyclones, which would mean both floating production platforms would have to disconnect and travel out of the path of the storm.
Production has been stopped as a precaution.
Both fields stopped output last week in the face of a similar tropical low and in recent months have been plagued by weather related problems.
